name: First Cook County court-house

documented_range.note: THE SEASON, THE MONTH AND THE CORNER ARE ALL FIXED BY ANDREAS, AND THEY DATE THIS BUILDING OUT OF THE SCENE. Until 2026-08-16 this record read 'NO SOURCE REACHED FIXES A MONTH' and modelled the court-house as complete on 1835-07-01, on the ground that a building finished somewhere in a twelve-month window is about half likely to be finished by 1 July. The window was never twelve months. Andreas's town-period narrative states it plainly: 'During the fall of the year (1835,) a one-story and basement brick court-house was erected on the northeast corner of the square, on Clark and Randolph streets. The county offices were in the lower story; the court-room, which was above, being one oblong apartment, capable of seating two hundred persons' (Andreas I scan p. 369). His chronological index carries the same building under the year 1835 at the month of NOVEMBER - 'court-house erected one story and basement, corner Clark and Randolph Streets' (scan p. 1317). And a third passage corroborates the season from a different direction, through a person rather than a building: R. J. Hamilton, elected Recorder at the August election, 'removed his office toward the end of October to the new building recently erected by the county on the public square' (scan p. 305). Three statements - a narrative, an index and a biography - and not one of them is earlier than the fall. THE PREVIOUS CITATION WAS A PICTURE. This record cited 'a section headed THE FIRST COURT-HOUSE. at scan p. 373'; scan p. 373 is a PLATE - the words are an engraving's caption, printed under 'Copyright secured by A. T. Andreas, 1884.' - and the narrative that carries the date is four scan pages earlier. The from date, 1835-10-01, IS A BOUND AND NOT A DATE, taken the way log_jail's is: the middle of a northern-Illinois autumn, on the earliest reading of 'fall' the end-of-October move-in allows. The chronology's November would put it a month later, and nothing here turns on which, because the scene date is 1 July and every reading is after it. THE END IS A HOUSEKEEPING BOUND. The caption's span, 1835-1853, is the building's documented life and is recorded here rather than in the range, because an eighteen-year phase would assert no change of fabric across the years Chicago changed faster than any settlement in America - which is the condition the validator's own wide-range rule exists to catch. ROADMAP T-I3.

position.symbolic_location: North-east corner of the public square (the block bounded by Randolph, Clark, Washington and LaSalle), at the Clark and Randolph end - the corner Andreas gives for this building, in the sentence that dates it and again in his chronology.
position.note: INVENTED WITHIN A DOCUMENTED BLOCK, AND THE CITATION TRAIL IS WHY THIS IS CONJECTURAL RATHER THAN INFERRED. This project's dossier, docs/research/04-structures-south.md line 178, tags the reading '1835, generally placed at the southwest corner of Clark & Randolph / on the public square; a small wooden stockade-type building' as [DOC] from the Illinois Court History PDF. THAT DOCUMENT DOES NOT CONTAIN IT: data/sources/illinoiscourthistory.json records that its entire 1835 content is one sentence and a caption, with no location, no corner, no material and no dimension, and that the corner and the description must be carried by Andreas or by nothing. Andreas is cited in the same dossier row for a SECTION HEADING only. So no source held by this project places this building on the square at all, let alone at a corner of it, and the placement below is a reasoned invention. WHAT IT IS REASONED FROM. The square existed to carry the county's buildings and already carried two of them - the estray pen at its south-west corner and the log jail at its north-west corner, both documented - so a court-house of 1835 belongs on that block on the balance of type. The corner adopted is the NORTH-EAST, for two reasons that point the same way and one that undercuts them: the reading in circulation, 'the southwest corner of Clark and Randolph', describes the corner of an INTERSECTION and therefore the north-east corner of the block; and the two documented structures occupy the west corners. THE UNDERCUT IS SERIOUS AND IS THE REASON FOR THE CONFIDENCE TAG: Andreas's well-known description of the court-house 'on the northeast corner of the public square' is the 1837 BUILDING, so the very siting adopted here is the one an 1837 description would contaminate an 1835 record with. It is adopted anyway, with that stated, because the alternative is to place the building somewhere with no argument at all. METHOD: the square's inside corners were computed from modern OpenStreetMap intersection centres fetched 2026-08-11 - Randolph and Clark at EPSG:26916 E 447651.47, N 4637142.45 - offset 12.2 m into the block on each axis, half of an 80 ft street per Hathaway 1834; the building's own north-east corner is set on the square's north-east corner. WORKING UNCERTAINTY ABOUT 20 M from the georeference, plus the width of the block, about 100 x 112 m, if the corner is wrong. Bearing 0 is a convention; nothing attests which way it faced. *** AMENDED 2026-08-16 (ROADMAP T-I3): THE UNDERCUT ABOVE IS REFUTED AND THE CORNER IS ATTESTED FOR THIS BUILDING. The claim that 'Andreas's well-known description of the court-house on the northeast corner of the public square is the 1837 BUILDING' does not survive reading the passage: Andreas's town-period narrative gives the north-east corner to THIS court-house, in the sentence that dates it - 'During the fall of the year (1835,) a one-story and basement brick court-house was erected on the northeast corner of the square, on Clark and Randolph streets' (Andreas I scan p. 369) - and his chronology repeats the corner under 1835 at the month of November, again as 'one story and basement' (scan p. 1317). So the corner this record reasoned its way to is the corner the source gives, and 'no source held by this project places this building on the square at all' was true only of the pages the record had looked at. THE GRADE IS NOT CHANGED IN THIS PARCEL and the reason is mechanical rather than evidential: this record no longer resolves into the 1835 scene, and a promotion here would be a change nobody can see, made in the same commit as the date correction that made it invisible. It belongs in the parcel that applies the fabric too, which needs a bake. See docs/RESEARCH/civic_public_buildings_1835.md. *** APPLIED 2026-09-27 (T-1687). THE CORNER IS TAKEN, AND THE GRADE FOLLOWS THE WEAKER HALF OF IT. The amendment above parked this reading on the ground that a promotion belonged in 'the parcel that applies the fabric too, which needs a bake'. That pricing stopped being true five weeks ago and the record says so itself, further down: T-0139 retired this record's committed GLB on 2026-08-23 because the bake cannot reach a phase no scene resolves, and the research note ends 'There is no mesh to stale.' So the corner has been free to apply since then and nobody applied it - the parcel was still waiting for a bake that had been abolished. IT IS APPLIED NOW. The corner is ATTESTED for THIS building, twice: the town-period narrative dates it and sites it in one sentence - 'During the fall of the year (1835,) a one-story and basement brick court-house was erected on the northeast corner of the square, on Clark and Randolph streets' (Andreas I scan p. 369) - and the chronology repeats the corner under 1835 at November (scan p. 1317). The coordinate is DERIVED, from the same OpenStreetMap intersection centres and the same 12.2 m half-street offset the estray pen and the log jail were placed from, so the tag reads `inferred` on exactly the rule estray_pen states for the same block: 'THE CORNER IS DOCUMENTED AND THE COORDINATE IS DERIVED, so the tag follows the weaker half'. NOT ONE NUMBER MOVES. The building's north-east corner sat on the square's north-east corner before this amendment and sits there after it; utm_e, utm_n and the bearing are untouched, and the record draws nothing either way. What moves is what the record CLAIMS: from a reasoned invention that admitted its one siting detail might be an 1837 description leaking backwards, to the corner the source gives for this building. And the `symbolic_location` moves, because it read 'no source reached fixes the corner' - which has been false since 2026-08-16, the day the narrative was read, on the same record that refuted it two paragraphs above.

derivation.reason: This placement predates the derivation module. Its provenance and reasoning are recorded in position.note, but no machine-checkable derivation block has been authored for it yet.

footprint.note: INVENTED, AND THE NUMBER YOU WERE EXPECTING IS A DIFFERENT BUILDING. NO SOURCE REACHED GIVES THIS STRUCTURE ANY DIMENSION AT ALL. 7.315 x 5.486 m is 24 x 18 ft, recorded converted with the original figures stated per data/datum.json's units rule; the size is chosen as a plain one-room court for a county seat of about 3,265 people, larger than the log jail across the block and smaller than any of the three worship buildings. THE TWO DESCRIPTIONS THAT MUST NOT REACH THIS POLYGON, both recorded here so that nobody re-adds them: (1) 'about thirty by sixty feet ... front ornamented with a four-column Doric portico of wood work' is Andreas on the 1837 COURT-HOUSE - thirty by sixty feet with a portico is a different building, and it is the description everyone reaches for; (2) 'constructed in the Greek Revival style, and built with stone ... designed by the architectural firm of John M. Van Osdel' sits two lines under the 1835 sentence in illinoiscourthistory and belongs to the 1853 court-house - Van Osdel did not reach Chicago until 1837. The second is the easier mistake and is why data/sources/illinoiscourthistory.json exists in the form it does.

construction.note: INVENTED. The phrase 'a small wooden stockade-type building' circulates in this project's dossier tagged to a document that does not contain it (see the position note), so even 'wooden' is carried here without a citation. Plank - sawn boards on a light frame - is the value in this archetype's vocabulary that claims the least: it says only what a viewer would see, which is a boarded wall. Log is the live alternative and would be the reading if 'stockade-type' turns out to be sourceable, since a stockade is uprights set in the ground. Brick and stone are excluded by date rather than by taste: the first brick building in Chicago is 1837. *** AMENDED 2026-08-16 (ROADMAP T-I3): ANDREAS SAYS BRICK, AND THE DATE ARGUMENT AGAINST BRICK IS ABOUT A HOUSE. 'During the fall of the year (1835,) a one-story and basement BRICK court-house was erected on the northeast corner of the square' (Andreas I scan p. 369), and the chronology's entry for the same building says 'one story and basement' (scan p. 1317). The reasoning recorded above - 'Brick and stone are excluded by date rather than by taste: the first brick building in Chicago is 1837' - is about the first brick HOUSE, P. F. W. Peck's, which this project already excludes as peck_brick_house; a brick county building in the fall of 1835 precedes it and Andreas records both. THE VALUE IS NOT CHANGED IN THIS PARCEL because changing a graded form value stales the placeholder mesh and geometry belongs to the nightly bake, and because the record no longer resolves into the 1835 scene, so nothing is drawn from it either way. Andreas also gives the plan: 'The county offices were in the lower story; the court-room, which was above, being one oblong apartment, capable of seating two hundred persons.' *** APPLIED 2026-09-27 (T-1687), WITH THE CONSEQUENCE STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER. The value is now `brick` at `attested`, on the sentence quoted above, and the reasoning that held it at invented `plank` is retired: it rested on 'the first brick building in Chicago is 1837', which is about P. F. W. Peck's brick HOUSE - already excluded here as peck_brick_house - and Andreas records the county's brick court-house of the fall of 1835 in the same volume. The two reasons this was parked are both gone. The bake is gone: T-0139 retired this record's committed mesh on 2026-08-23, so there is no placeholder geometry for a changed form value to stale, which `validate.py --stale` confirms on this commit. And 'nothing is drawn from it either way' is a reason to leave the record WRONG, not a reason to leave it alone: a record that says INVENTED plank where its source says brick misrepresents what this project knows, and that is the one thing the tiers exist to prevent. THE CONSEQUENCE, SAID OUT LOUD: `outbuilding` cannot build brick. Its vocabulary is log, plank and light_frame (generators/archetypes/outbuilding_params.py CONSTRUCTIONS), so the first scene that ever covers the fall of 1835 will resolve this phase and the archetype will refuse the value. That refusal is CORRECT and is left in place deliberately: the crosswalk's I3 canonical archetype is `institution_civic`, which does not exist yet, and choosing the archetype for a one-story-and-basement brick county building with its court room over its offices is a geometry decision for the parcel that builds it - not something to pre-empt by keeping the fabric wrong. `validate.py --params` resolves no phase for this record today, which is why the tree is green with the attested value in place.

wall_height_m.note: INVENTED. 3.0 m is about 10 ft to the plate - enough for a court room with a bench and a jury in it, and a little more than the 8 ft 9 in this record's neighbour the log jail carries. Nothing attests a height, a storey count or a ceiling. The archetype refuses a storey count outright for this family of buildings, which is the right refusal here: two storeys of court-house is a claim, and nobody has made it for 1835. *** AMENDED 2026-09-27 (T-1687): THE STOREY COUNT IS ATTESTED NOW, AND THE VALUE STILL IS NOT. 'Nobody has made it for 1835' was wrong about the plan and right about the number. Andreas gives the plan twice - 'a one-story and basement brick court-house', and 'the county offices were in the lower story; the court-room, which was above, being one oblong apartment, capable of seating two hundred persons' (scan p. 369) - so what is attested is one principal storey over a basement, with the court room above and the offices below, and NOT two storeys of wall standing on the ground. 3.0 m is kept as the invention it is: it is the height of the principal storey to the plate, the basement is below grade and no archetype here models one, and no source gives a figure for either.

roof_type.note: INVENTED. Nothing attests a roof of any kind. Gable is what a small wooden public building of the period and region carried, and it is what the archetype would default to at this depth in any case; it is stated rather than defaulted so that the confidence view can show it as the invention it is.

roof_pitch_deg.note: INVENTED. 32 degrees is this archetype's own default for a gable, kept deliberately rather than replaced with a fresh guess, on the reasoning docs/LIBERTIES.md L29 states about the bridge's pier spacing: a new number would look like a finding and would not be one.

door.note: INVENTED. door in this archetype names what has to get through the opening. People went into a court-house and nothing else did, so the man-door class is the reading; nothing attests a door, its position or its size. A public building might well have had a double leaf, which this class does not build.

phases.change_note: The first Cook County court-house, erected on the public square in the fall of 1835. IT DOES NOT STAND IN THE 1835 SCENE, AND THAT IS WHAT THIS RECORD IS NOW FOR. It was modelled as complete on 1835-07-01 from 2026-08-11 until 2026-08-16, when T-I3 read the Andreas narrative this record had only ever cited a caption from, and found the season, the month and the corner all attested - every one of them after the scene date. The record is kept and dated rather than deleted: the building is real, this project is year-parameterized, and a record that resolves into 1836 and not into 1835 is how that is said. THE TWO AMENDMENTS IT PARKED ARE APPLIED, 2026-09-27 (T-1687): the north-east corner is attested for this building and the record now claims it at `inferred` - documented corner, derived coordinate - and the fabric is `brick` at `attested`. Both were held back in August on the ground that a changed form value stales a mesh and geometry belongs to a bake; T-0139 retired the mesh five days later and nothing came back for them.

function.note: 'Cook County built their first courthouse in 1835', and the caption 'The first Cook County Courthouse, 1835-1853'. That is the entire documentary basis for this structure's existence and function in the sources this project holds, and it is enough for both. THE SAME PAGE SUPPLIES NOTHING ELSE - no dimension, no material, no storey count, no roof, no portico, no location, no month - and the two descriptions sitting near it belong to the 1837 and 1853 buildings; see the footprint note. *** AMENDED 2026-09-27 (T-1687): ANDREAS IS THE SECOND AND BETTER BASIS, AND HE IS NOW CITED HERE. 'That is the entire documentary basis for this structure's existence and function in the sources this project holds' was true of the pages the record had read on 2026-08-11 and stopped being true on 2026-08-16, when the town-period narrative was read: it names the building, its county, its fabric, its plan, its corner and its season in one sentence. The function is unchanged; what changes is that the record no longer rests it on a caption and a single sentence.

research_note: THE MOST UNCERTAIN RECORD IN THIS PARCEL, AND IT IS ON THE PROJECT'S WATCH LIST FOR A REASON. data/exclusions.json's watch_list already states the problem exactly: the year is documented, no source fixes a month, so on 1835-07-01 the building may be unbuilt, under construction, or just finished. This record builds it complete and tags everything about it conjectural except its existence, its year and its function. THREE GUARDS TRAVEL WITH IT AND ALL THREE ARE ABOUT DESCRIPTIONS OF OTHER BUILDINGS. (1) THE 1837 BUILDING: Andreas's 'court-house on the northeast corner of the public square, basement and principal story, about thirty by sixty feet, court-room and jury rooms on the principal floor, clerk's and recorder's offices and vaults in the basement, front ornamented with a four-column Doric portico of wood work' is 1837. Do not attach it. Note the sting in the tail - this record adopts the north-east corner of the square on independent reasoning, which means the ONE siting detail it does assert is also the one the 1837 description would contaminate it with. (2) THE 1853 BUILDING: in illinoiscourthistory the sentences run 'Cook County built their first courthouse in 1835. The county's second courthouse (and city hall) was built in 1853. It was constructed in the Greek Revival style, and built with stone ... designed by ... John M. Van Osdel.' The 'It' is the 1853 building. A reader skimming for the first court-house finds a Greek Revival stone building two lines under it, and Van Osdel did not reach Chicago until 1837. (3) THE DOSSIER'S OWN OVER-TAGGING: docs/research/04-structures-south.md line 178 tags the corner and the phrase 'a small wooden stockade-type building' as [DOC] from the Illinois Court History PDF, and that document contains neither. Nothing in this record cites them. WHAT WOULD UPGRADE THIS RECORD, in order of value: the Cook County commissioners' records for 1834-35, which would carry a contract, a cost, a specification and a completion date and would settle the month, the material and the size in one document; Andreas vol. 1 at page-image level around scan p. 373, under the heading 'THE FIRST COURT-HOUSE.', which this session has not read; and any of the five works illinoiscourthistory lists in its own bibliography without citing to a page - Goodspeed 1909, Andreas 1884, Currey 1912, Carter 1914, Goeldner 1970. A single dated county order would move this record from conjectural to documented across four attributes at once. *** NO MESH IS COMMITTED FOR THIS RECORD, AND THAT IS DELIBERATE (T-0139, 2026-08-23). The phase runs 1835-10-01 to 1835-12-31 and the only scene targets 1835-07-01, so generators/build.py resolves no phase for this record and builds nothing for it; the scene sidecar already reports it as '1 excluded by date' and no renderer loads it. Its GLB was nevertheless committed and input-hashed like every other asset, which made it a trap rather than a spare: any edit to generators/build.py or generators/common/ restales the whole town, and the full rebake that heals the other 344 assets CANNOT reach this one - so the tree could not be made green by any committed route. It cost T-0008 a throwaway script that monkey-patched resolve_phase, and cost T-0015 a demonstrated export guard that was reverted rather than patched past a second time. The asset was therefore retired and tools/validate.py::run_bake_reach_check now refuses any committed asset the bake cannot reach. NOTHING IS LOST: the geometry is a function of this record, and the moment a scene covers the fall of 1835 the ordinary bake will build it. It also unblocks the two amendments this record parks - the Andreas readings of BRICK construction and of the north-east corner, both held back on the ground that changing a graded form value would stale a mesh that needed a bake. There is no mesh to stale. *** THE AMENDMENTS ARE APPLIED, 2026-09-27 (T-1687), AND THE SENTENCE ABOVE IS WHY THEY COULD BE. This record parked the Andreas readings of the north-east corner and of brick construction on a bake that T-0139 had already abolished, and the paragraph above says so in terms - 'It also unblocks the two amendments this record parks ... There is no mesh to stale.' Nobody came back for them for five weeks, because the place that tracked them was docs/RESEARCH/civic_public_buildings_1835.md section 7, which still priced them as needing a bake. Both are applied now and section 7 is closed. WHAT IS STILL OWED AFTER THIS, and it is not a citation: the archetype. `outbuilding` cannot build brick, so the first scene to cover the fall of 1835 will refuse this phase rather than build a plank court-house - which is the failure this project wants, in the place it wants it. The corner's coordinate also still overhangs Randolph Street as the plat module draws the block, which tools/measure_reserved_ground.py prints in its own docstring and reads as 1 of 4 corners in; it is a consequence of seating the building's corner ON the block's corner, it is unchanged here, and it is a placement question for the same parcel.
